Why not only build the tests for the allowed daemons?

Not all features/daemons are enabled by default, so if we did that we'd need a solution for CI to build everything.  Additionally, if unit tests are a unit, there shouldn't be any downside to running them (except compile times for a build-all build).
if there's a better option here, I'm open to it, I just don't see what it is.

> Not all features/daemons are enabled by default

Why not though? What's the concern?

I think having the set of tests built be consistent with the set of daemons enabled is a fairly reasonable philosophy and shouldn't be difficult to implement.

> > Not all features/daemons are enabled by default
> 
> Why not though? What's the concern?

I should clarify, they're not all enabled at a yocto level, so this is mostly moot in this context.

> 
> I think having the set of tests built be consistent with the set of daemons enabled is a fairly reasonable philosophy and shouldn't be difficult to implement.

That's something we could discuss, but that's not what's implemented today.  I'm not sure I agree with you at this stage (given the unit tests are pretty fast to both build and run) but I could certainly see a case where we need that some day if the unit tests get too lengthy to build.  If it's ok, I'd like to see that as a separate initiative (ideally done by someone that wants to see that happen, maybe that's you?).  I'm not sure I could properly defend it today.

https://github.com/openbmc/dbus-sensors/blob/master/src/tests/meson.build

Everything in the test repo is currently enabled unconditionally.

I think we can handle enabling the tests based on feature as a followup patch and reduce the scope of this patch to just moving the meson option check into subfolders (by updating patch comment description to reflect so).
@andrew@codeconstruct.com.au you good with that, or do you want to keep this patch in review until this is addressed?
Switching to feature-based tests in a follow-up is fine.
Appreciate the feedback.

> not recursiving into
the subdirectory prevents compilation if both unit tests are enabled and
the feature is disabled.

I don't think so, recursing into a subdirectory is not required for meson to use the files therein.

```
test(
    'MCTPEndpoint',
    executable(
        'test_MCTPEndpoint',
        'test_MCTPEndpoint.cpp',
        '../mctp/MCTPEndpoint.cpp',
        dependencies: [gmock_dep, ut_deps_list, utils_dep],
        implicit_include_directories: false,
        include_directories: '../mctp',
    ),  
)
```

mctp test is defined like above, and even with
```

  User defined options
    mctp                    : disabled
    nvidia-gpu              : enabled
    nvme                    : disabled
```

the mctp tests can build

```
meson test
ninja: Entering directory `/home/alexander/upstreaming/dbus-sensors/build'
ninja: no work to do.
1/5 test_utils          OK              0.04s
2/5 test_ipmb           OK              0.03s
3/5 MCTPReactor         OK              0.02s
4/5 MCTPEndpoint        OK              0.02s
5/5 NvidiaGPU           OK              0.01s

Ok:                5   
Fail:              0   
```
Correct, it's not required to use the files, but it is required to use any dependencies or variables within, which could be reused.
If that's the actual reason, it makes more sense to me now. Thanks for explaining.

We can use `subdir_done()` to avoid all the extra indentation.

https://mesonbuild.com/Reference-manual_functions.html#subdir_done

something like

```
if not get_option('tests').allowed()
  subdir_done()
endif
```

If it works for you we could apply throughout the patch.

I wasn't aware of that method.  Seems reasonable, I'm not sure i'll have time to make that patch soon, but I can try.  Can you try 1 quick example from this patch and see if subdir_done() solves this in a way that's acceptable to you?
I tried with `mctp` and `nvidia-gpu` and for both cases it works and results in less diff and indentation.
ACK, will implement when I get a moment.
Done

Unit tests are disabled in yocto - https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/blob/master/meta-phosphor/recipes-phosphor/sensors/dbus-sensors_git.bb#L103. 

If unit tests are only enabled while running ci on this repo, all the features will also be enabled and it would not cause a problem?
The issue comes up in development, where nvidia-gpu has been disabled.
Done
Should be also consider moving test files themselves to feature subdirectories?
They were just moved out recently.  Happy to consider going back, but not in this commit.
Done

nit: extra newline in diff here,

and in a few other files as well.
I'm fairly certain more files end in newline than not;  Is this an issue that we should hold this patch up for?

> Is this an issue that we should hold this patch up for?

not really. Whenever i prefix a comment with `nit:` it's a nitpick and probably not super important to me.

Should i mark the comment as resolved in those cases?

I find nits can be useful to improve the patch if the author makes another revision due to other reason. In that case they can address the nitpicks as well since they are already uploading a new revision anyways.
Yep, I agree with the "nit" approach, I'm just making sure you'd ok with this going forward without them.
